samples.summary: OOXML attribute injection sink left unsealed by the sweep: `anim.durationMs` / `anim.delayMs` / `anim.pptxPreset.id` are interpolated raw into `<p:cTn dur=…>`, `presetID=` and `<p:cond delay=>`
samples.evidence: Attack: a caller with write access to a deck PUTs `slides[0].animations = [{ elementId: <an id that exists on the slide>, start: 'onClick', category: 'entrance', effect: 'fadeIn', durationMs: "500\"><p:evil/><p:cTn id=\"0\" dur=\"1" }]`. The backend never validates `slide.animations` — `assertValidSlide` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:518-558) checks only id/layoutId/background/elements/notes — and `writeSlidesRoot` stores the slide object verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:105). No read-side codec normalizes it (grep for `durationMs` in packages/slides/src finds no migration). On PPTX export, `slideToXml` calls `animationsToTimingXml(slide.animations ?? [], spidMap)` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/slide.ts:163) and `effectParXml` emits `` `<p:cTn id="0" dur="${anim.durationMs}" …` `` (animation.ts:221), `` presetID="${presetID}" `` (line 222, where presetID = the persisted `pptxPreset.id`) and `` delay="${anim.delayMs ?? 0}" `` (line 223) with no coercion and no escaping — unlike the sibling values `presetClass`/`presetSubtype` on the same lines, which ARE run through `escapeXmlAttr`. The string closes the attribute and injects attacker-chosen elements/attributes into ppt/slides/slideN.xml of any .pptx a victim later exports (`renumberCTnIds` is a plain regex and does not sanitize). Every other numeric sink in the exporters is safe because it passes through `Math.round`/`pxToEmu*` (NaN, not a string) — these three are the exception.

samples.summary: New `assertValidSlideInlines` accepts `inlines` absent and `inline.style` absent, but shared slides consumers dereference both unconditionally — a single PUT persistently breaks rendering/export for every viewer
samples.evidence: The guard returns early when `inlines` is undefined/null (line 742) and only checks `style` when it is present (lines 760-768), unlike the docs arm which requires `Array.isArray(b.inlines)` (line 419) and a present object `style` (line 437). But `packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:209-210` does `for (const inline of block.inlines) { if (inline.style.fontFamily) … }` over blocks read straight back from the deck — a stored block with no `inlines` throws 'not iterable', and an inline with no `style` throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined'. `packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:197` (`resolveColorAtPosition`) likewise reads `inline.style.color` and is called on every caret paint from `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:578`, the editor slides text boxes use. Attack: an authenticated collaborator PUTs `{... elements:[{type:'text', data:{blocks:[{style:{}, inlines:[{text:'x'}]}]}}] }`; the endpoint accepts it (style-less inline is explicitly tolerated), `writeSlidesRoot` persists it verbatim, and thereafter PDF export and text-box editing throw for every viewer of that deck — a persistent, non-self-healing DoS on the document. The guard's own docstring gives 'throws for every viewer of that deck' as the reason it exists, so the tolerance defeats half of its stated purpose.
searchedFor: grep writeSlidesRoot in packages/backend/src/yorkie to confirm verbatim persistence

samples.summary: `themeToXml` now normalizes `theme.colors[role]` but still assumes `theme.name`, `theme.fonts.heading/body` and the `colors`/`fonts` containers themselves are present strings; the backend validates `themes` only as an array
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlidesBody` checks `Array.isArray(b.themes)` and nothing more (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:472-478), and `writeSlidesRoot` persists the array verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:102). `escapeXmlAttr` is `s.replace(...)` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/xml.ts:5), so a PUT of `themes:[{id:'t',colors:{},fonts:{heading:42}}]` makes `escapeXmlAttr(theme.fonts.heading)` throw a TypeError at theme.ts:103, and a theme with no `colors` object throws at `theme.colors[role]` (line 97) — PPTX export of the deck fails for every viewer. Not injection (the values are escaped when they are strings), but the same untrusted-input reasoning the new `toSrgbHex` docstring applies to `colors` was not extended to its siblings on the same object.

samples.summary: Object-literal attribute lookups the Map sweep skipped: `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` and animation.ts's `TYPE_TO_TAG`/`DIR_TO_ATTR`/`START_TO_NODE_TYPE` still resolve through the prototype chain
samples.evidence: `colorChildXml` does `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` and interpolates the result into `<a:schemeClr val="…">` (color.ts:49-50); `transitionToXml` does `TYPE_TO_TAG[t.type]` into an element NAME position `<p:${tag}…>` (animation.ts:90,99) and `DIR_TO_ATTR[t.direction]` into `dir=` (line 95); `START_TO_NODE_TYPE[anim.start]` goes raw into `nodeType=` (line 221). All four keys come from persisted JSON the content PUT API never validates, so `role: 'constructor'` / `type: '__proto__'` yields an inherited `Object.prototype` member stringified into the output. I could not turn this into injection — the inherited values contain no `"` or `<` — so the impact is a malformed part rather than attacker-chosen XML, but these are exactly the lookups the delta converted elsewhere (docx-style-map.ts, connector.ts, layout.ts, shape.ts) and leaving them reads as covered when it is not.

[], spidMap)` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/slide.ts:163) and `effectParXml` emits `` `<p:cTn id="0" dur="${anim.durationMs}" …` `` (animation.ts:221), `` presetID="${presetID}" `` (line 222, where presetID = the persisted `pptxPreset.id`) and `` delay="${anim.delayMs ?? 0}" `` (line 223) with no coercion and no escaping — unlike the sibling values `presetClass`/`presetSubtype` on the same lines, which ARE run through `escapeXmlAttr`. verdict.reason: The described sink exists verbatim: animation.ts:221-223 interpolates `anim.durationMs`, `presetID` (from `anim.pptxPreset.id`, assigned at line 187) and `anim.delayMs` into `<p:cTn dur=…>`, `presetID=` and `<p:cond delay=>` with no coercion and no escaping, while the sibling `presetClass` (222) and `presetSubtype` (198) and `motionPath` (210) on the same block DO go through `escapeXmlAttr` — so the three named values are genuinely the exception, not a pattern I misread. The path is reachable from untrusted input: `assertValidSlide` (docs-content.controller.ts:518-558) validates only id/layoutId/background/elements/notes and never touches `animations`, the surrounding payload walk (472-496) only descends into slides' elements/notes and layouts' placeholders/staticElements, and the read path in yorkie-slides-store.ts:435-445 passes `animations` through `yorkieToPlain` and spreads it unmodified — the TS type is the only 'guard' and it is erased at runtime. Export then reaches it at slide.ts:163 via `animationsToTimingXml(slide.animations ?? [], spidMap)`, and `renumberCTnIds` (slide.ts:164) is only an id-renumbering regex, not a sanitizer. Result: a writer can persist a string durationMs that closes the attribute and injects attacker-chosen elements into ppt/slides/slideN.xml of any .pptx a victim later exports. This is injection / unsafe input handling, squarely in the security lane, and I found no guard anywhere on the write, storage, read, or export path.

verdict.reason: The factual chain checks out: assertValidSlideInlines (docs-content.controller.ts:741-770) does tolerate absent `inlines` and absent `style`, unlike the docs arm (:419, :437); pdf.ts:209-210, docs/src/model/color.ts:192-201 and slides/src/model/element.ts:654 dereference `block.inlines` / `inline.style` unguarded; and nothing normalizes on read (migrate.ts:121-168 touches only meta/background/shape fills, text-renderer.ts:261-264 normalizes only block.style, slides-tree.ts:97-109 stores verbatim). So the absence is real — I found no counterexample. It is however not a Security-lane defect. The actor required is exactly the actor the endpoint already authorizes for total destruction: WorkspaceScopeGuard (workspace-scope.guard.ts:26-36) admits any workspace member / workspace-scoped API key, writeSlidesRoot is a documented destructive replace (slides-tree.ts:83-105), and assertValidSlidesBody (docs-content.controller.ts:472-482) fully accepts `slides: []`, letting the same caller blank the whole deck for every viewer through the validated path and restore it just as easily. The tolerance therefore crosses no privilege boundary and grants no capability the endpoint does not already grant. It matches none of this lens's lane items (authz bypass, secrets, injection, crypto/auth, SSRF, deserialization, traversal); it is a missing defensive null-check causing a TypeError in renderers — an availability/robustness bug belonging to the correctness lens, which reviewed this exact validator (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:3). Refuted on scope, not on facts.

finding.summary: `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}">` is still interpolated raw in the very function the diff hardened against attacker-chosen alignment values
finding.evidence: The diff routes `<w:jc w:val>` through the closed `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` map and adds a design-doc table claiming "every value-typed attribute is therefore resolved through a converter that can fail closed" (docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md §3.3). Ten lines above the new lookup, `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` still does `parts.push(`<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>`)` with neither `escapeXmlAttr` nor a converter, guarded only by `if (headingLevel)` — any non-empty string is truthy. `block.headingLevel` is untrusted at the same level `alignment` is: the v1 content PUT validator (`assertValidBlock`, docs-content.controller.ts:360-443) checks `id`/`type`/`style`/`inlines` and never looks at `headingLevel`, so `PUT .../content` with `{blocks:[{id:'b',type:'heading',headingLevel:'1"/><w:jc w:val="right', style:{}, inlines:[]}]}` stores it verbatim. Attacker: a workspace member poisons a shared doc; any other member exporting DOCX gets attacker-chosen OOXML (e.g. field codes) in word/document.xml, header1.xml and footer1.xml. I could not complete the chain end-to-end: both CRDT readers coerce it (`Number(attrs.headingLevel)` at packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:396 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:473), so today the string arrives at the exporter as NaN and the sink emits `HeadingNaN`. The sink is therefore unexploitable-by-accident rather than injection-proof, which is exactly the property the diff set out to establish here — hence low confidence, major impact if a caller ever reaches DocxExporter without the CRDT round-trip (note `putContent` echoes the raw request body back rather than re-reading, docs-content.controller.ts:175).

verdict.reason: The finding claims `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` still does `parts.push(`<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>`)` guarded only by `if (headingLevel)`. That code is not in the working tree. docx-style-map.ts:139-144 defines `toHeadingStyleId`, a closed converter that returns `undefined` unless `Number(headingLevel)` is an integer in 1..6, and docx-style-map.ts:155-158 interpolates the converter's output (`headingStyleId`), not the raw `headingLevel`, under `if (headingStyleId)`. The only reachable values are the six literals Heading1..Heading6, which contain no XML metacharacters, so the `<w:pStyle w:val>` attribute cannot be closed by attacker input. The finding's specific payload `'1"/><w:jc w:val="right'` coerces to NaN, fails `Number.isInteger`, and the element is dropped — contradicting the finding's own claim that the sink emits `HeadingNaN`; the converter fails closed rather than passing NaN through, so the stated residual risk (a caller reaching DocxExporter without the CRDT round-trip) is already covered at the sink. A repo-wide grep for `pStyle w:val="Heading` finds the raw-interpolation form only in an archived planning doc (docs/tasks/archive/2026/04/20260410-docx-import-export-todo.md:2061) and a test fixture string (packages/docs/test/import/docx-parser.test.ts:145), neither of which is compiled export code; grepping `pStyle|headingLevel` across packages/docs/src/export shows line 157 is the only `<w:pStyle>` emission, and its sole caller docx-exporter.ts:188 routes through it. The design-doc row the finding cites (docs-docx-import-export.md:440) matches the shipped behavior. Ground: not-present.
